Direct INSERT: issuedAt = dbNow + 1 s -> 'observed execution grant expired'; expiresAt = dbNow (issuedAt = dbNow - 25 s) -> 'observed execution grant expired'; expiresAt - issuedAt = 30001 ms -> 'observed execution grant invalid'. No existing INSERT-path pin of these messages was found (grep of src/test outside GuidedPublicationReplayIT: only the retry-rebind 'grant invalid' at GuidedSecretLoginMigrationTest), so they are added, not duplicated. cases.theDatabaseClockReadsClockTimestampInAnd: DatabaseClock contract. Outside a transaction: instant() is within the bracketing clock_timestamp() reads and isActualTransactionActive() stays false. Inside a TransactionTemplate: instant() within the bracket; two reads 50 ms apart differ by >= 50 ms; SELECT now() stays equal to its transaction-start value while the clock moves on. Zone is UTC.

negativeControlMethod.how: The checkout was never edited for the controls. An out-of-tree Gradle init script compiled the old (or skewed) configuration classes into a scratch directory, assembled a scratch copy of the main classes with those two classes swapped, and pointed only the Test task's runtime classpath at that copy. compileJava stayed UP-TO-DATE and build/classes/java/main was not modified: the sha256 of the two compiled configuration classes (9d1608e2..., 3a51921d...) was identical before and after both control runs. The 'restore byte-identical' step is therefore vacuous: the source files were never changed, and their sha256 matched the post-edit values after the controls.
negativeControlMethod.firstAttemptAborted: An earlier version of the overlay excluded the two sources from compileJava and added the overlay sources to it. It failed twice (attempt 1: the init script also reached buildSrc, compile error; attempt 2: context failure, no ObservedRevisionVerifier bean). After attempt 2 the two configuration .class files were missing from the shared build/classes/java/main. They were recompiled at 14:10:18 local by a Gradle run this lane did not launch. javap then showed both referencing DatabaseClock, and every later run of this lane used them. Inference, not proven: attempt 2's compile-input change removed them. That approach was abandoned for the classpath-only method above.

deviations.what: The ruling expected the literal negative control (Clock.systemUTC() restored) to make case (3) fail through the trigger. It did not, and case (2) does not discriminate under it either.
deviations.why: Verified by the run, with an inferred explanation. The old wiring hard-coded Clock.systemUTC(), so the test's offset application Clock bean never reached it. In this run the host clock agreed with the Docker VM clock (the ruling's probe measured within about 1 ms), so the old Java check also refused a grant expired 1 ms ago by the DB clock as 409. To show that case (3) detects a JVM-judged expiry, the supplementary negSkewed control ran the old wiring with its JVM clock 788 s behind. Cases (1), (2) and (3) then failed, (3) with the JpaSystemException the ruling predicted. Case (1) is the deterministic wiring pin. It failed under both controls.
